title: Inventory Consignment Dispute
question_for_arbitration: Verdant Micro Corp. is seeking an order directing Teletronics Inc. to immediately pay the principal amount of $143,000.00, plus applicable interest and arbitration fees. The basis for this claim is a direct violation of Section 9.2 of the Teletronics Consignment Agreement, under which Teletronics failed to forward gross third-party customer receipts to Verdant "without deduction," opting instead to entirely withhold the funds.
arbitration_clause: This arbitration shall be administered by DecisionLayer.AI under its Foundational + Strict Contractual Ruleset, subject to the law of New York and the Federal Arbitration Act. The arbitration will be held online through DecisionLayer.ai. Both parties agree to resolve any claims relating to or arising out of these Terms or the Services through final and binding individual arbitration by a single arbitrator. Class arbitrations, class actions, private attorney general actions, and consolidation with other arbitrations are not allowed. The arbitrator may award relief only individually and only to the extent necessary to redress individual claims. The DecisionLayer rules will govern payment of all arbitration fees. Dropbox will not seek its attorneys' fees and costs in arbitration unless the arbitrator determines that the claim is frivolous or brought for an improper purpose.

Consignment Agreement
This Consignment Agreement (this "Agreement"), dated as of [DATE], is entered into by and between Verdant Micro Inc., a Delaware corporation having its principal place of business at 450 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10022 ("Consignor"), and Teletronics Inc., a Pennsylvania corporation having its principal place of business at 1200 Commerce Drive, Harrisburg, PA 17101 ("Consignee," and together with Consignor, the "Parties," and each, a "Party").
Recitals

Consignor is in the business of supplying the products identified in Schedule 1 (the "Goods").
Consignee is in the business of selling telecommunications devices and components.
Consignee wishes to obtain from Consignor, and Consignor wishes to deliver to Consignee, certain quantities of Goods for the purpose of sale by Consignee to third parties (the "Consigned Goods") in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement.
In consideration of the mutual covenants, terms, and conditions in this Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
1.	Appointment.
1.1	Consignor appoints Consignee, and Consignee accepts the appointment, to serve as a non-exclusive Consignee to sell the Consigned Goods to third-party purchasers identified by Consignee ("Customers") pursuant to the terms and conditions of this Agreement. Consignor may in its sole discretion sell goods other than the Consigned Goods, directly or indirectly, to any third party.
1.2	This Agreement does not preclude either Party from entering into an agreement with any third party to market and sell other goods, including those that compete with the Consigned Goods.
1.3	If Consignee becomes aware of any actual or potential claim against Consignor, Consignee shall promptly notify Consignor.
2.	Consignment Requests, Confirmations, and Forecasts.
2.1	Consignee shall issue one or more orders, consignment requests, or similar documents to Consignor to request the delivery of Consigned Goods (each a "Consignment Request") via email or by using EDI. Each Consignment Request shall specify the following commercial terms:
(a)	a list of the Goods to be consigned, including make, model number, and SKU;
(b)	the quantities ordered;
(c)	the requested delivery date, which shall be no less than 14 days after the Consignor's receipt of the Consignment Request; and
(d)	the applicable shipping term and delivery point.
2.2	Within 5 days following receipt of a Consignment Request, Consignor shall issue to Consignee a confirmation document ("Consignment Confirmation") that sets forth the quantity and type of Consigned Goods to be delivered to Consignee, price that Consignee may provide to Customers for the Consigned Goods, and other relevant commercial terms such as the delivery date and applicable shipping term and delivery point. If the Consignor does not accept a Consignment Request within such period, the Consignment Request is deemed to be rejected by the Consignor.
2.3	The terms of this Agreement prevail over any terms or conditions contained in any other documentation, including any terms or conditions in the Consignment Request or Consignment Confirmation.
2.4	No later than 30 days before the last day of each calendar quarter, Consignee shall notify Consignor of its good faith forecast of the quantities of the Goods by type that it expects to order from Consignor each month during the following 6 month period. The forecasts are for information purposes only and do not create a binding obligation on either Party.
3.	Delivery and Storage.
3.1	Consignor shall deliver to Consignee's facility located at 1200 Commerce Drive, Harrisburg, PA 17101 (the "Facility") such quantities of Consigned Goods as Consignee may request from time to time as set forth in the applicable Consignor Confirmation.
3.2	Consignee shall inspect the Consigned Goods promptly after delivery and notify Consignor in writing of any discrepancy in the quantity, condition, or quality of any Consigned Goods ("Nonconforming Goods") within 10 days after delivery. Consignee may return any Nonconforming Goods to Consignor at Consignor's cost, provided that Consignee notifies Consignor in writing at least 5 days prior to such return.
3.3	Consignee shall store all Consigned Goods in a manner that protects them from damage or deterioration. Consignee shall store the Consigned Goods in areas segregated from all other goods and property (the "Segregated Area") and shall clearly identify them as the property of Consignor by conspicuous sign or placard. Such identification and marking shall include marking one or more units of Consigned Goods in each lot.
3.4	Consignee represents and warrants that the Facility is appropriate for the storage of goods such as the Consigned Goods and is free from hazards and damage of any nature that could affect the Consigned Goods. If either Party believes or has reason to believe that the Facility is no longer appropriate for the proper storage of the Consigned Goods, the Parties shall, by mutual agreement, locate another facility suitable for the storage of the Consigned Goods. Consignee is responsible for maintaining the Facility throughout the term of this Agreement in such a manner as to remain suitable for the storage of the Consigned Goods, including maintaining appropriate insurance coverage.
3.5	Consignor shall have the right to inspect the Facility during the Facility's regular business hours upon 3 days' prior written notice to Consignee.
3.6	Consignee shall keep an accurate record of all Consigned Goods in its possession. Consignor and its representatives shall have access to such records and the right to make inventories of the Consigned Goods in the possession of Consignee during normal business hours upon 3 days' prior written notice to Consignee.
4.	Title and Risk of Loss.
4.1	Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Consignor shall retain title to the Consigned Goods until Customer purchases and takes possession of the Consigned Goods, at which time title to the Consigned Goods shall pass directly from Consignor to the Customer.
4.2	Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement:
(a)	Consignor assumes the risk of loss, theft, or damage to the Consigned Goods until the Consigned Goods are delivered to the Facility. Consignor shall replace or repair at its cost any Consigned Goods that are lost, stolen, or damaged before they are delivered to the Facility.
(b)	Notwithstanding Section 4.1, Consignee assumes the risk of loss, theft, or damage to the Consigned Goods upon delivery to the Facility. Consignee shall pay Consignor the replacement cost of the Consigned Goods that are lost, stolen, or damaged after delivery to the Facility.
5.	Consignor's Security Interest in Consigned Goods. Without derogating from Consignor's rights as owner of the Consigned Goods, Consignee:
5.1	Grants to Consignor as security for the payment of the purchase price of the Consigned Goods, as and when due, a purchase money security interest in all of Consignee's right, title, and interest in and to the Consigned Goods and all proceeds thereof.
5.2	Shall cooperate with and assist Consignor in connection with establishing and maintaining Consignor's: (i) title to the Consigned Goods, and (ii) priority of ownership interest in and to such Consigned Goods as against claims of secured and unsecured creditors of Consignee.
5.3	Authorizes Consignor, pursuant to Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code ("UCC"), to file UCC financing statements as Consignor may deem appropriate to perfect its interest in the Consigned Goods and proceeds thereof, and to take such other steps as may be necessary to secure Consignor's rights in and to the Consigned Goods.
5.4	Shall assist Consignor in fulfilling any and all notice requirements for the purpose of maintaining its priority ownership interest in and to the Consigned Goods.
6.	Liens, Encumbrances, and Indemnity. Consignee shall maintain the Consigned Goods free and clear of and from and against all liens and encumbrances of any nature whatsoever. Consignee shall indemnify and hold harmless Consignor from and against any loss or damage caused by acts of Consignee, whether or not authorized by this Agreement, which result in any liens or encumbrances being placed upon any Consigned Goods, including all costs, fees, and expenses incurred by Consignor in commencing or participating in proceedings as are necessary for Consignor to defend its ownership interest in the Consigned Goods.
7.	Return of Consigned Goods.
7.1	Consignor may require that Consignee return any Consigned Goods delivered and not yet sold by Consignee. Consignee shall promptly return such goods in accordance with Consignor's reasonable instructions. Consignor shall bear the risk of loss and the expense of returning the Consigned Goods.
7.2	Consignee may, with prior written notice to Consignor, return Consigned Goods that it has not sold. Consignee shall bear the risk of loss and the expense of returning the Consigned Goods.
8.	Marketing Obligations.
8.1	Consignee shall, at its expense, market, advertise, promote, and solicit the sale of the Consigned Goods to prospective and existing customers in a manner that is consistent with Consignor guidelines.
8.2	Consignor shall provide any information, material, and support that Consignee may reasonably request to enable Consignee to market, advertise, promote, and solicit the sale of Consigned Goods under this Agreement.
8.3	Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Consignee shall not make, directly or indirectly, any representations or warranties on behalf of Consignor or with respect to the Consigned Goods, except as expressly authorized by Consignor or set forth in Consignor's literature and promotional materials.
9.	Customer Orders, Payment, and Delivery.
9.1	Consignee shall promptly forward to Consignor all Customer sales inquiries, requests for quotations, and purchase orders. All orders solicited by Consignee shall be subject to acceptance or rejection by Consignor, in whole or in part, at Consignor's sole discretion.
9.2	Consignee shall forward to Consignor without deduction any amounts received from Customers for the Consigned Goods.
9.3	If a Customer requires the Consigned Goods to be delivered to the Customer's facilities, Consignee shall coordinate delivery with the Customer. Consignor shall reimburse Consignee for all reasonable and documented delivery charges incurred by Consignee in connection with delivery of the Consigned Goods to Customers.
10.	Commissions.
10.1	Commission Rate. Subject to Section 10.2, Consignee shall earn commissions ("Commissions") for completed sales of the Consigned Goods that were solicited by Consignee at the rate of 8 percent (8%) of the Net Sales Price under the applicable Customer contract. For the purposes of this Agreement, "Net Sales Price" means the gross invoice price less all taxes, shipping, handling, and insurance charges.
10.2	Commission Payment Terms. Commissions are earned and payable to Consignee 15 days after the last day of the month in which Consignor receives unconditional payment under the corresponding Customer contract (each, a "Payment Date").
10.3	Monthly Reports. Consignor shall keep records of all completed sales of Consigned Goods through Consignee hereunder and submit to Consignee with each payment a report ("Monthly Report") indicating: (i) all sales during the applicable month for which Consignee has earned Commissions pursuant to Section 10.2; (ii) the price of the Consigned Goods provided to Customers and the payments received by Consignor with respect to such sales; and (iii) the amount of Commissions due to Consignee on the Payment Date. Consignee shall notify Consignor in writing of any dispute regarding any Monthly Report within 30 (thirty) days after receipt of such Monthly Report. Consignee shall have access to such records to verify the accuracy of the monthly recommission payments during normal business hours upon 5 days' prior written notice to Consignor.
10.4	Payment of Commissions on Termination. After the termination of this Agreement, Consignor shall continue to pay Commissions to Consignee on Customer orders for Consigned Goods received prior to the termination date for which Customer payments are received within 90 days after the termination date.
11.	Compliance with Laws. Each Party shall at all times comply with all laws and regulations applicable to the operation of its business, this Agreement, and its performance hereunder.
12.	Intellectual Property.
12.1	Ownership. Consignee acknowledges and agrees that Consignee shall not acquire any ownership interest in any patents, trademarks, copyrights, domain names, works of authorship, trade secrets, or any other intellectual property (collectively, "Intellectual Property") owned by or licensed to Consignor under this Agreement. 12.2	Trademark License Grant. 13.	Term. The term of this Agreement commences on the date first set out above and shall continue for an initial term of one year unless sooner terminated pursuant to Section 14. After the end of the initial term, this Agreement will be automatically renewed for successive one-year periods.
14.	Termination. Either Party may terminate this Agreement with or without cause by providing written notice to the other Party at least 30 (thirty) days prior to the end of the initial term or a renewal term.
15.	Confidentiality. This Agreement constitutes the sole and entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter contained herein, and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous understandings, agreements, representations, and warranties, both written and oral, regarding such subject matter.

All notices under this Agreement shall be made in writing and shall be deemed duly given if delivered either in person, by certified or registered mail, return receipt requested and postage prepaid, or by recognized overnight courier service. All notices shall be addressed to the Parties at their respective addresses first set forth above (or to such other address that the receiving Party may designate from time to time in accordance with this section).
